svg.title: RIEMANN R1 — Main.lean, theorem by theorem: the five theorems, the statements they are made of, and the chain of reductions that proves them
svg.desc: The formal proof is 164,464 Lean files with no comments; the blueprint reads it as 416 statements and the edges between them. This diagram draws the five theorems of Main.lean, the definitions they are stated with, and the chain of reductions by which the hard one, GRH, half-plane form, reaches the theorems that the chapters prove. Each node is one blueprint statement: the Lean declaration it stands for, as the blueprint's facts file records its signature, the statement in words, how its proof goes, and what it uses and is used by. Read it from the foot up: the five theorems are at the bottom, and everything above is what their proofs use. No Lean was built for the blueprint or for this diagram: the edges were resolved from the source text and some are wrong, and whether the formal proof is correct is a question for the kernel checks of band 5.

∀ (s : ℂ) (_ : riemannZeta s = 0) (_ : ¬∃ n : ℕ, s = -2 * (n +
The Riemann Hypothesis is the statement that every zero s of the Riemann zeta function other
than the trivial zeros -2, -4, -6, … satisfies Re s = 1/2. Here ζ is defined on all of ℂ and
given an arbitrary value at its pole s = 1, so the statement also excludes s = 1.
Blueprint main-theorems/def-riemann-hypothesis.md (The main theorems) · depth 1 from the

text.tspan: Non-vanishing right of the critical line

svg.text: ∀ (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) (s : ℂ), 1 / 2
We say that Dirichlet L-functions do not vanish right of the critical line if for every modulus N ≥
1, every Dirichlet character χ modulo N, primitive or not, and every s with Re s > 1/2, L(χ,
s) ≠ 0, the pole χ = 1, s = 1 excepted.

text.tspan: Zeros in the critical strip lie on the line

svg.text: ∀ (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) (s : ℂ),
We say that the zeros of Dirichlet L-functions in the critical strip lie on the line if for every
modulus N ≥ 1 and every Dirichlet character χ modulo N, every zero of L(χ, s) with 0 < Re
s < 1 has Re s = 1/2. We use the same phrase restricted to primitive characters.

text.tspan: The five stages of the proof (the architecture chapter's own list)

svg.text: Galois representations (chap-galois). To every polarized regular algebraic cuspidal representation of GL_a over a CM field we attach a Galois representation, compatible with a weak form of the local
The Tate–Shafarevich bound (chap-sha). These representations bound the Tate–Shafarevich groups of the twists Q_l/Z_l(-e) over the abelian fields that a Dirichlet character ψ cuts out of a 2-power

Families (chap-families). For each primitive ψ and each large x, an auxiliary CM field of degree about x^2 carries families of definite unitary groups of growing rank, linked by theta lifts and carrying
hermitian lattices (thm-family-data-exists). The theta lifts and the Siegel–Weil formula (chap-theta) and a covolume bound from arithmetic heights (chap-heights) give the families their properties …

Slope data and the core inequality (chap-zero-free). The families give a slope inequality for the hermitian lattices at primes inert in the auxiliary field. Averaged along a chain of theta lifts, it bounds a
weighted von Mangoldt sum G_m(x) by x^(1/2 + O(ε)) (thm-core-inequality).
Landau's theorem (chap-zero-free). The bound holds on windows [Y, Y^(3/2)] of arbitrarily large Y, and Landau's theorem on Dirichlet series with non-negative coefficients turns it into a zero-free

Read right to left: each theorem reduces the half-plane claim to the one on its left, and GRH from Galois representations gathers the whole chain. An arrow from A to B says that the proof of B uses A.
Suppose that the Tate–Shafarevich bound holds with exponent 401, and that some class of
families satisfies the family hypotheses (def-family-data). Then no L-function of a primitive
character vanishes right of the critical line (def-zero-free-primitive), and hence Dirichlet L
-functions do not vanish right of the critical line.
Apply thm-zero-free-from-connected with windows of exponent λ = 3/2. Its two
hypotheses are slope data for the families, which thm-families-connected gives, and
auxiliary fields, which thm-auxiliary-fields gives from the Tate–Shafarevich bound at
each ψ. thm-primitive-suffice passes from primitive characters to all.
proof in outline) · depth 3 from the main theorems

If polarized pairs have Galois representations (def-galois-reps-polarized), then Dirichlet L
-functions do not vanish right of the critical line (def-nonvanishing-half-plane).
Assume that polarized pairs have Galois representations. The proof walks down the chain of
From these Galois representations, thm-sha-bound (chap-sha) gives the Tate–Shafarevich
bound with exponent 401 for every primitive character, and thm-local-parameters-exist
gives a system of local parameters. These are the hypotheses of thm-grh-from-sha-bound.
By the theorem of Gelfand and Kazhdan, the Galois representations of polarized pairs give
Galois representations for the cuspidal representations that the families use (
sec-gal-cuspidal). This reduces the claim to thm-grh-from-theta-integrals.
With these, thm-family-data-exists (chap-families) gives a class of families of definite
unitary groups satisfying the family hypotheses. Its inputs come from chap-theta,
chap-heights and chap-sha. This reduces the claim to thm-zero-free-from-families.

Statements by depth from the main theorems (the diagram's own count)

svg.text: A statement's depth is the fewest uses edges from one of the three theorems nothing else uses (The Riemann
Hypothesis and the two critical-line forms) down to it. The five theorems of Main.lean sit at depths 0 and 1.
7 of the blueprint's 416 statements are reached by no edge from the main theorems: the blueprint's remarks
and a few results whose users it did not resolve.
Published results sit mostly at depths 4 and 5: the new argument is the top of the tree and rests on the

text.tspan: Checked and proved: what is known about the formal proof

svg.text: lake build Main compiles every file of the submission; a successful build is a check by the kernel of Lean v4.33.1, the version the project pins.
The mirror's notes list independent complete builds, and compare their compiled files with the checksums the author published: in the complete
lake comparator exports the five theorems and replays them in kernels independent of Lean's own, Lean paranoid and nanoda, allowing only
the three axioms of comparator.json. The notes say its output will be added when the run finishes. At the state drawn, no result is recorded.
No Lean was built for the blueprint. Its uses edges were resolved from identifiers in the source text, and its README says some are wrong and
that every proof status reads *absent*. This diagram inherits both limits. A node here says what a statement is, not that it is proved.
